source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice long questions written from Chapter 14 (PDF 18-44), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 14 (Simple Harmonic Motion) ke poore chapter se practice long questions (tafseeli sawal) hain, Board ke long question ki shakal mein: har 5 number ke theory sawal (definition, wazahat, derivation) ke baad usi mauzu ka 3 number ka numerical hai. Har sawal ka model jawab hai; numericals qadam ba qadam hal kiye gaye hain.

blocks.prompt:
1 Define vibration, amplitude, time period, frequency and angular frequency. Starting from the definition of angular frequency, show that ω = 2π/T = 2πf. (5 marks)
(Vibration, amplitude, time period, frequency aur angular frequency ki definitions likhein. Angular frequency ki definition se shuru kar ke dikhayein ke ω = 2π/T = 2πf.)
blocks.explanation:
Vibration: mean position ke gird vibrate karne wale jism ka aik mukammal chakkar (cycle), jaise pendulum ke bob ka A se B aur wapas A tak jaana.

Amplitude (x₀): mean position ke kisi bhi taraf zyada se zyada displacement ki miqdaar (OA = OB = x₀).

Time period (T): aik vibration mukammal karne ka waqt. SI unit: second (s).

Frequency (f): aik second mein mukammal vibrations ki tadaad: f = n/t = 1/T. Unit: hertz (Hz), yani aik oscillation fi second; dimension [T⁻¹].

Angular frequency (ω): fi unit waqt angular displacement:
ω = θ/t
Aik chakkar mein θ = 2π radian aur t = T, is liye
ω = 2π/T
f = 1/T hai, is liye
ω = 2πf
aur T = 1/f = 2π/ω. ω ki SI unit: rad s⁻¹; dimension [T⁻¹].

book_ref.quote: Time period in terms of frequency f and angular frequency ω is expressed as:

blocks.prompt:
2 A vibrating body completes 45 vibrations in 18 s. Find (i) its frequency (ii) its time period (iii) its angular frequency. (3 marks)
(Vibrate karta jism 18 s mein 45 vibrations karta hai. (i) frequency (ii) time period (iii) angular frequency nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Frequency fi second vibrations hai; T us ka ulat; ω = 2πf.

book_ref.quote: Frequency is defined as the number of vibrations or oscillations (n) completed by the vibrating body in one second

blocks.final_answer: f = 2.5 Hz, T = 0.4 s, ω = 15.7 rad s⁻¹

blocks.prompt:
3 State the conditions necessary for simple harmonic motion. Using Hooke's law and Newton's second law, show that a body attached to a spring on a smooth horizontal surface has an acceleration directly proportional to its displacement and directed towards the mean position. What role does inertia play? (5 marks)
(Simple harmonic motion ki zaroori sharait bayan karein. Hooke's law aur Newton ke doosre qanoon se dikhayein ke hamwar ufuqi sateh par spring se bandhe jism ka acceleration displacement ke directly proportional aur mean position ki taraf hota hai. Inertia ka kya kirdaar hai?)
blocks.explanation:
S.H.M ki sharait (14.2):
• Restoring force mean position se displacement ke directly proportional ho.
• Force aur displacement Hooke's law, F = −kx, par chalein.
• Acceleration displacement ke proportional ho, a ∝ −x; manfi nishaan batata hai ke yeh mean position ki taraf hai.

Mass-spring system: m mass ka jism k constant wale spring se hamwar ufuqi sateh par bandha hai; O mean position hai (Fig. 14.2). Force F usay O se A tak x hataati hai. Hooke's law se:
F ∝ x, yani F = kx ... (14.1)
Spring barabar magar ulti simt mein elastic restoring force lagata hai:
F = −kx ... (14.2)
Newton ke doosre qanoon se:
F = ma ... (14.3)
(14.2) aur (14.3) ko milayein:
ma = −kx, yani a = −(k/m)x ... (14.4)
k/m constant hai, is liye a ∝ −x.
Yehi S.H.M ki riyazi shakal hai: acceleration displacement ke seedhe tanasub mein aur manfi nishaan ki wajah se hamesha mean position ki taraf.

Inertia (jumood) ka kirdaar: Chhorne par jism O ki taraf aata hai. O par force sifar hai, magar inertia ki wajah se jism O se aage B tak jaata hai, spring dabata hai aur laut aata hai; is tarah A aur B ke beech oscillate karta rehta hai. Restoring force khud sirf displacement par munhasar hai, inertia par nahi.

book_ref.quote: Consider a body of mass 'm' attached with a spring of spring constant 'k' lying on smooth horizontal surface

blocks.prompt:
4 A 0.3 kg body is attached to a spring of constant 120 N m⁻¹ on a smooth horizontal surface. It is pulled 5 cm to the right and released. Find the restoring force and the acceleration of the body at the moment of release. (3 marks)
(0.3 kg jism hamwar ufuqi sateh par 120 N m⁻¹ spring se bandha hai. Usay 5 cm daayen khench kar chhora gaya. Chhorte lamhe restoring force aur acceleration nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Force ke liye F = −kx, phir a = −(k/m)x; nishaan simt batata hai.

book_ref.quote: The negative sign shows that acceleration and displacement are always in opposite direction

steps: Manfi nishaan: force aur acceleration baayen, mean position ki taraf.
blocks.final_answer: F = 6 N aur a = 20 m s⁻², dono mean position ki taraf

blocks.prompt:
5 By comparing the acceleration of a mass-spring system with a = −ω²x, obtain expressions for its angular frequency, frequency and time period. Explain how the time period changes with the mass and with the stiffness of the spring, and name some real-world uses of S.H.M. (5 marks)
(Mass-spring system ke acceleration ko a = −ω²x se mila kar us ki angular frequency, frequency aur time period ki expressions nikalein. Wazahat karein ke time period mass aur spring ki sakhti ke saath kaise badalta hai, aur S.H.M ke kuch amli istemal batayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Mass-spring system ke liye (Eq. 14.4):
a = −(k/m)x
Har S.H.M ke liye (Eq. 14.8):
a = −ω²x
Dono ko milayein:
ω² = k/m, yani ω = √(k/m)
Frequency: ω = 2πf se
f = ω/2π = (1/2π)√(k/m)
Time period: T, f ka ulat hai,
T = 1/f = 2π√(m/k)

Inhisaar:
• T ∝ √m: bhaari mass lamba period (chaar guna mass, do guna period).
• T ∝ 1/√k: sakht spring (zyada k) chhota period aur zyada frequency.
• T amplitude par munhasar nahi.

S.H.M ke amli istemal: pendulum clocks, musical instruments aur gaariyon ka suspension system.

book_ref.quote: T is the reciprocal of f = (1/2π)√(k/m), so m/k comes under the root

blocks.prompt:
6 A 0.6 kg mass oscillates on a spring of constant 150 N m⁻¹. Find (i) its angular frequency (ii) frequency (iii) time period. (3 marks)
(0.6 kg mass 150 N m⁻¹ spring par oscillate karta hai. (i) angular frequency (ii) frequency (iii) time period nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Pehle ω = √(k/m), phir f = ω/2π aur T = 1/f.

book_ref.quote: The last line should read T = 1/f = 2π√(m/k)

blocks.prompt:
7 Resolve the weight of the bob of a simple pendulum at its extreme position and identify the restoring force. Using the small-angle approximation (support it from Table 14.1), show that the bob executes S.H.M, and derive its frequency and time period. (5 marks)
(Simple pendulum ke bob ka weight extreme position par components mein todein aur restoring force pehchanein. Chhote angle ki takhmeen (Table 14.1 se taeed karein) se dikhayein ke bob S.H.M karta hai, aur us ki frequency aur time period derive karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Simple pendulum: m mass ka chhota bhaari bob jo ℓ lambi halki inextensible dori se rigid support se latka ho.

Forces: Extreme position P par weight mg dori se θ angle banata hai (Fig. 14.3 b). Components: dori ke saath mg cosθ aur amoodan mg sinθ. Dori ke rukh motion nahi, is liye mg cosθ tension T se cancel hota hai. mg sinθ mean position ki taraf restoring force hai:
F = −mg sinθ
Newton ke qanoon F = ma se
ma = −mg sinθ, a = −g sinθ ... (14.5)

Chhota angle: chhote angles par sinθ ≈ θ (radians mein). Table 14.1 yeh dikhata hai: 5° = 0.0873 rad aur sin 5° = 0.0872. Is liye
a = −gθ ... (14.6)
θ = S/ℓ (S = arc ki lambai) se a = −(g/ℓ)S. Chhote angle (taqreeban 10° ya kam) par x ≈ S, to
a = −(g/ℓ)x ... (14.7)
ℓ aur g muqarrar hon to g/ℓ constant: a ∝ −x. Is liye simple pendulum ki motion S.H.M hai.

Frequency aur period: a = −ω²x (14.8) se milayein:
ω² = g/ℓ, ω = √(g/ℓ) ... (14.9)
ω = 2πf se: f = (1/2π)√(g/ℓ)
T = 1/f = 2π√(ℓ/g) ... (14.10)
T √ℓ ke seedhe, √g ke ulte tanasub mein, aur bob ke mass aur (chhote) amplitude se azaad hai.

book_ref.quote: We can resolve weight into its rectangular components.

blocks.prompt:
8 A simple pendulum is 1.6 m long. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², find its (i) angular frequency (ii) time period (iii) frequency. (3 marks)
(Simple pendulum 1.6 m lamba hai. g = 9.8 m s⁻² le kar (i) angular frequency (ii) time period (iii) frequency nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: ω = √(g/ℓ), phir T = 2π/ω aur f = 1/T.

book_ref.quote: The above expression shows that the time period of simple pendulum is directly proportional to the square root

blocks.prompt:
9 Describe how a simple pendulum is used to determine the acceleration due to gravity at a place. Why should the amplitude be kept small? What is a second pendulum, and would the same pendulum keep the same period on the Moon? (5 marks)
(Bayan karein ke simple pendulum se kisi jagah gravity ka acceleration kaise maloom kiya jaata hai. Amplitude chhota kyun rakhna chahiye? Second pendulum kya hai, aur kya wohi pendulum Chaand par wohi period rakhega?)
blocks.explanation:
Tareeqa: Simple pendulum ka time period
T = 2π√(ℓ/g) ... (14.10)
Square karein: T² = 4π²ℓ/g, is liye
g = 4π²ℓ/T²
Pendulum ki lambai ℓ naapein. Chhote amplitude se jhulaayein aur stopwatch se time period T naapein (durustagi ke liye kai vibrations ka waqt le kar un ki tadaad se taqseem karein). ℓ aur T rakh kar us jagah g nikalein.

Chhota amplitude kyun: T = 2π√(ℓ/g) mein sinθ ≈ θ aur x ≈ arc S istemal hue jo sirf chhote angles (taqreeban 10° ya kam) par durust hain. Tab hi a ∝ −x aur motion isi period ke saath S.H.M hai.

Second pendulum: jo aik vibration do second mein kare (T = 2 s). g = 9.8 m s⁻² par ℓ = gT²/4π² = 0.994 m.

Chaand par: T ∝ 1/√g. Chaand par g kam hai, is liye usi lambai ka pendulum wahan lamba period dega; waqt durust nahi rakhega.

book_ref.quote: The simple pendulum can be used to determine the gravitational acceleration at a particular location.

blocks.prompt:
10 A simple pendulum of length 0.90 m makes 20 complete vibrations in 38.2 s. Find the time period and the value of g at that place. (3 marks)
(0.90 m lamba simple pendulum 38.2 s mein 20 mukammal vibrations karta hai. Time period aur us jagah g ki qeemat nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Kul waqt ko vibrations se taqseem kar ke T, phir g = 4π²ℓ/T².

book_ref.quote: The time period T of the simple pendulum is measured using a stopwatch

blocks.prompt:
11 Describe how the shadow of a ball on a rotating turntable shows the link between S.H.M and uniform circular motion. Taking a particle P moving on a circle of radius x₀ with uniform angular velocity ω, derive the instantaneous displacement and instantaneous velocity of its projection Q, and find where the velocity is maximum. (5 marks)
(Bayan karein ke ghoomte turntable par gend ka saaya S.H.M aur uniform circular motion ka taalluq kaise dikhata hai. x₀ radius ke circle par yaksaan ω se ghoomte particle P ke projection Q ka instantaneous displacement aur instantaneous velocity derive karein, aur batayein ke velocity kahan zyada se zyada hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Turntable: r radius ke turntable ke rim par gend lagi hai. Table constant ω se ghoome to gend uniform circular motion karti hai. Roshni ki shuaa us ka saaya screen par daalti hai; saaya spring wale jism ki tarah aage peeche S.H.M karta hai (Fig. 14.4). Yani uniform circular motion ka diameter par projection S.H.M karta hai.

Set-up: P x₀ radius ke circle par yaksaan ω se ghoomta hai; us ki linear velocity vₚ = x₀ω tangent ke rukh hai. Q, P ka diameter par projection hai jo O ke gird oscillate karta hai.

Instantaneous displacement: P agar A se chale to t waqt mein radius OP θ = ωt angle tay karta hai (Fig. 14.5). Tikon POQ mein:
OQ/OP = cos θ, yani x/x₀ = cos ωt
x = x₀ cos θ = x₀ cos ωt ... (14.11)

Instantaneous velocity: Q ufuqi chalta hai, is liye us ki velocity vₚ ka horizontal component hai (Fig. 14.6):
v = vₚ cos(90° − θ) = vₚ sinθ
v = x₀ω sinθ = x₀ω sin ωt ... (14.12)
sinθ = √(1 − cos²θ) aur cosθ = x/x₀ se:
v = x₀ω√(1 − x²/x₀²)
v = ω√(x₀² − x²) = √((k/m)(x₀² − x²)) ... (14.13)

Zyada se zyada velocity: mean position x = 0 par:
v_max = x₀ω = √(k/m) x₀ ... (14.14)
Extreme positions x = ±x₀ par v = 0.

book_ref.quote: Therefore, as Q vibrates horizontally, so instantaneous velocity of the point Q is horizontal component

blocks.prompt:
12 A body in S.H.M has amplitude 0.12 m and angular frequency 6 rad s⁻¹. Find (i) its maximum speed (ii) its speed when the displacement is 0.072 m. (3 marks)
(S.H.M mein jism ka amplitude 0.12 m aur angular frequency 6 rad s⁻¹ hai. (i) zyada se zyada speed (ii) 0.072 m displacement par speed nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Zyada speed mean position par x₀ω; x par v = ω√(x₀² − x²).

book_ref.quote: Eq. (14.13) should read v = ω√(x₀² − x²)

steps: x₀ = 0.12 m, ω = 6 rad s⁻¹, x = 0.072 m
blocks.final_answer: v_max = 0.72 m s⁻¹; x = 0.072 m par v = 0.576 m s⁻¹

blocks.prompt:
13 Derive the instantaneous acceleration of the projection of a particle moving on a circle with uniform angular velocity, and hence show that the projection executes S.H.M. Where is the acceleration maximum and where is it zero? (5 marks)
(Yaksaan angular velocity se circle par ghoomte particle ke projection ka instantaneous acceleration derive karein aur dikhayein ke projection S.H.M karta hai. Acceleration kahan zyada se zyada aur kahan sifar hai?)
blocks.explanation:
P x₀ radius ke circle par yaksaan ω se ghoomta hai aur Q us ka diameter par projection hai jo centre O se x faasle par hai.

P ka acceleration aₚ centripetal hai, centre ki taraf, miqdaar x₀ω² (Fig. 14.7). Is ka horizontal component diameter ke saath hai, is liye Q ka acceleration aₚ ka horizontal component hai:
a = (aₚ)ₓ = aₚ cosθ
Centre ki taraf (x ke ulat) rukh ko manfi lein, aₚ → −x₀ω², aur cosθ = x/x₀:
a = −x₀ω²(x/x₀) = −ω²x
a = −xω² ... (14.15)
Manfi nishaan batata hai ke acceleration hamesha mean position ki taraf hai.

ω constant hai, is liye a ∝ −x. Yehi S.H.M ki riyazi shart hai. Is liye circle par ghoomte particle ka projection S.H.M karta hai.

Zyada aur sifar: |a| = ω²x extreme positions x = ±x₀ par zyada se zyada (x₀ω²) aur mean position x = 0 par sifar.

book_ref.quote: Thus, the acceleration of projection Q is equal to the horizontal component of aₚ.

blocks.prompt:
14 A particle moves on a circle of radius 0.25 m with a period of 2 s. Find the acceleration of its projection (i) when the projection is 0.10 m from the centre (ii) at an extreme position. (3 marks)
(Particle 0.25 m radius ke circle par 2 s period se ghoomta hai. Projection ka acceleration (i) jab projection centre se 0.10 m par ho (ii) extreme position par nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: ω = 2π/T, phir a = −ω²x; extreme par x = x₀.

book_ref.quote: This expression is the mathematical condition of S.H.M

steps: ω = 2π/2 = π rad s⁻¹, ω² = 9.87 s⁻²
Extreme x₀ = 0.25 m par: |a| = 0.25 × 9.87 = 2.47 m s⁻²
blocks.final_answer: (i) 0.987 m s⁻² centre ki taraf (ii) 2.47 m s⁻² centre ki taraf

blocks.prompt:
15 Define phase and phase constant. Using x = x₀ cos(ωt + φ), describe where the oscillating point is at t = 0, T/4, T/2, 3T/4 and T for φ = 0°, 90° and 180°. What is meant by oscillating in phase and out of phase? (5 marks)
(Phase aur phase constant ki definition likhein. x = x₀ cos(ωt + φ) se batayein ke φ = 0°, 90° aur 180° ke liye t = 0, T/4, T/2, 3T/4 aur T par oscillating point kahan hota hai. In phase aur out of phase oscillation se kya muraad hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Phase: woh angle θ = ωt jo S.H.M karte point ka displacement x aur motion ki simt batata hai; yeh oscillator ki motion ki haalat dikhata hai. Aam shakal:
x = x₀ cos(ωt + φ) ... (14.18)
Waqt ke saath badalne wali miqdaar (ωt + φ) motion ka phase hai. Constant φ phase constant (phase angle) hai; is ki qeemat t = 0 par particle ke displacement aur velocity par munhasar hai. φ do oscillators ki haalat ka phase difference bhi batata hai.

φ = 0°: x = x₀ cos ωt (Fig. 14.8 a). t = 0, T/2 aur T (θ = 0, π, 2π) par point extreme positions par; t = T/4 aur 3T/4 (θ = π/2, 3π/2) par mean position par.

φ = 90°: x = x₀ cos(ωt + 90°) (Fig. 14.8 b). t = 0, T/2 aur T par point mean position par; t = T/4 aur 3T/4 par extreme positions par.

φ = 180°: x = x₀ cos(ωt + 180°) (Fig. 14.8 c). t = 0 par point −x₀ (ulti extreme) par, T/4 aur 3T/4 par mean position par, T/2 par +x₀ par; graph φ = 0° wale graph ka ulta hai.

In phase: phase difference 0° ya 360°; dono system saath chalte hain.
Out of phase: phase difference 180°; jab aik +x₀ par ho to doosra −x₀ par.

book_ref.quote: The quantity φ represents the phase difference between the states of motion of two oscillators.

blocks.prompt:
16 A body oscillates according to x = 0.1 cos ωt (x in metres) with a time period of 1.2 s. At t = 0.2 s find (i) its phase (ii) its displacement (iii) the magnitude of its velocity. (3 marks)
(Jism x = 0.1 cos ωt (x metre mein) ke mutabiq 1.2 s time period se oscillate karta hai. t = 0.2 s par (i) phase (ii) displacement (iii) velocity ki miqdaar nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: ω = 2π/T; phase = ωt; phir x = x₀ cos ωt aur |v| = x₀ω sin ωt.

book_ref.quote: Where x is instantaneous displacement, x₀ is maximum displacement

blocks.prompt:
17 Write the expressions for the displacement, velocity and acceleration of a body executing S.H.M starting from an extreme position, and describe their graphs against time. State where each is maximum and zero, and give the phase differences between them. (5 marks)
(Extreme position se shuru hone wale S.H.M karte jism ke displacement, velocity aur acceleration ki expressions likhein aur waqt ke muqable un ke graphs bayan karein. Batayein ke har aik kahan zyada aur kahan sifar hai, aur un ke darmiyan phase differences batayein.)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Displacement:
x = x₀ cos ωt ... (14.19)
Graph (Fig. 14.9 a) cosine curve hai jo +x₀ se shuru hota hai. Displacement extreme positions par zyada se zyada (x₀) aur mean position par sifar.

(ii) Velocity: miqdaar
v = x₀ω sin ωt ... (14.20)
Nishaan samait, x = x₀ cos ωt ke liye v = −x₀ω sin ωt, is liye graph sifar se shuru ho kar pehle neeche jaata hai (Fig. 14.9 b). Velocity mean position par zyada se zyada (x₀ω) aur extreme positions par sifar.

(iii) Acceleration: a = −ω²x; x = x₀ cos ωt rakhein,
a = −x₀ω² cos ωt ... (14.21)
Graph (Fig. 14.9 c) −x₀ω² se shuru hota hai, displacement graph ka aaina-numa ulta. Acceleration extreme positions par zyada se zyada (x₀ω²) aur mean position par sifar.

Phase differences:
• Velocity aur displacement: π/2.
• Velocity aur acceleration: π/2.
• Acceleration aur displacement: π, kyun ke a = −ω²x unhein hamesha ulta rakhta hai.

book_ref.quote: The graphical representations of displacement, velocity and acceleration of a body executing SHM

blocks.prompt:
18 A body executes S.H.M according to x = x₀ cos ωt with x₀ = 0.05 m and ω = 8 rad s⁻¹. Find its displacement, velocity and acceleration at t = 0.1 s (angle in radians). (3 marks)
(Jism x = x₀ cos ωt ke mutabiq S.H.M karta hai, x₀ = 0.05 m aur ω = 8 rad s⁻¹. t = 0.1 s par displacement, velocity aur acceleration nikalein (angle radians mein).)
blocks.explanation: ωt radians mein nikalein; phir x = x₀ cos ωt, v = −x₀ω sin ωt, a = −ω²x.

book_ref.quote: The acceleration of the particle executing SHM is given by the expression:

blocks.final_answer: x = 0.0348 m, v = −0.287 m s⁻¹ (mean position ki taraf), a = −2.23 m s⁻²

blocks.prompt:
19 Using the average restoring force, find the work done in stretching a spring to its amplitude and hence the elastic potential energy of a mass-spring oscillator. Derive its kinetic energy at displacement x and prove that its total energy is constant. Express the total energy in terms of m and ω, and describe the energy graph. (5 marks)
(Average restoring force se spring ko amplitude tak khenchne ka kaam aur mass-spring oscillator ki elastic potential energy nikalein. Displacement x par kinetic energy derive karein aur sabit karein ke kul energy constant hai. Kul energy m aur ω ki shakal mein likhein aur energy graph bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Average force: Restoring force x = 0 par sifar aur x = x₀ par F = kx₀ hai, is liye
F_av = (0 + kx₀)/2 = ½kx₀
x₀ tak khenchne ka kaam:
W = F_av × x₀ = ½kx₀(x₀) = ½kx₀²
Yeh kaam elastic potential energy ki shakal mein jama hota hai. Kisi displacement x par:
(P.E.)inst = ½kx² ... (14.22)
x = 0 par sifar aur x = ±x₀ par zyada se zyada:
(P.E.)max = ½kx₀² ... (14.23)

Kinetic energy: v = ω√(x₀² − x²), ω = √(k/m):
v = √((k/m)(x₀² − x²)) ... (14.24)
x = 0 par v_max = √(k/m) x₀ ... (14.25)
K.E. = ½mv² = ½k(x₀² − x²) ... (14.26)
Mean position par P.E. = 0 aur saari energy kinetic:
T.E = K.E.max = ½mv²max = ½kx₀² ... (14.27)

x par kul energy:
T.E = K.E + P.E = ½k(x₀² − x²) + ½kx² = ½kx₀² ... (14.28)
Yeh x par munhasar nahi, is liye kul energy constant aur amplitude ke square ke proportional hai. k = mω² se:
T.E = ½mω²x₀²

Graph (Fig. 14.11): x ke muqable −x₀ se +x₀ tak, P.E. parabola jo centre par sifar, K.E. ulta parabola jo centre par zyada se zyada, aur T.E ufuqi seedhi line. Energy K.E. aur P.E. mein badalti hai magar majmooa constant rehta hai.

book_ref.quote: Thus, average value of force from the mean position to the extreme position is:

blocks.prompt:
20 A 0.4 kg mass on a spring of constant 160 N m⁻¹ oscillates with amplitude 5 cm. At x = 3 cm find its potential energy, kinetic energy and speed, and check that the total energy equals ½kx₀². (3 marks)
(0.4 kg mass 160 N m⁻¹ spring par 5 cm amplitude se oscillate karta hai. x = 3 cm par potential energy, kinetic energy aur speed nikalein, aur check karein ke kul energy ½kx₀² ke barabar hai.)
blocks.explanation: P.E. = ½kx², K.E. = ½k(x₀² − x²); speed K.E. = ½mv² se.

book_ref.quote: The total energy is the sum of kinetic and potential energy of the system at displacement

blocks.prompt:
21 Explain free oscillations, forced oscillations and damped oscillations with examples. Describe light, heavy and critical damping, and explain why shock absorbers are used in a car. (5 marks)
(Free oscillations, forced oscillations aur damped oscillations ko misalon ke saath wazeh karein. Light, heavy aur critical damping bayan karein, aur batayein ke car mein shock absorbers kyun lagaye jaate hain.)
blocks.explanation:
Free oscillations: Jab jism bairooni force ki madakhlat ke baghair apni natural frequency se oscillate kare. Misaal: thora hataya gaya simple pendulum apni lambai par munhasar natural frequency se azaadana jhoolta hai (Fig. 14.12). Rukawat na ho to kul energy aur amplitude constant rehte hain.

Forced oscillations: Azaad oscillating system par bairooni force lage to forced vibrations hoti hain. Misalein: baar baar dhakka diya gaya jhoola (Fig. 14.13); bhaari machinery se factory ka farsh; string instruments ke lakri ke boards.

Damped oscillations: Amalan hawa ki rukawat aur friction jaisi forces energy zaaya karti hain. Rukawat ki forces ki maujoodgi mein ghatte amplitude wali oscillations damped oscillations aur yeh forces damping forces kehlati hain. Misaal: jhoole par larki ka amplitude kam hota jaata hai aur jhoola ruk jaata hai (Figs. 14.14, 14.15); vibrate karte tuning fork ko chhoona.

Damping ki qismein:
• Light damping: energy aur amplitude aahista kam, jaise playground ka jhoola.
• Heavy damping: jism ke rukne mein zyada waqt, jaise gaarhe tail mein pendulum.
• Critical damping: jism kam se kam waqt mein equilibrium par, jaise car ke shock absorbers.

Shock absorbers: Kharab raaste par car ka suspension bohat zyada oscillate karta. Shock absorbers in oscillations ko damp karte hain (Fig. 14.16) taake musafiron ka safar aaraam deh ho.

23 What is resonance? Describe an experiment with pendulums of different lengths hung from a horizontal rod to demonstrate it. Explain how resonance is used in a microwave oven and in tuning a radio, and why soldiers break step on a bridge. (5 marks)
(Resonance kya hai? Ufuqi rod se latke mukhtalif lambai ke pendulums wala tajruba bayan karein jo resonance dikhata hai. Wazahat karein ke microwave oven aur radio tuning mein resonance kaise kaam aati hai, aur sipahi pul par qadam kyun torte hain.)
blocks.explanation:
Forced oscillation: Damped oscillator par periodic bairooni (driving) force lage to amplitude constant reh sakta hai; is ki frequency driving frequency hai. Amplitude driving frequency aur natural frequency ke taalluq par munhasar hai.

Resonance: Jab driving force ki frequency jism ki natural frequency ke barabar ho to vibration ka amplitude bohat barh jaata hai. Yeh resonance (gunj) hai.

Tajruba (Fig. 14.17): Pendulums A aur B (lambai ℓ₁) aur C aur D (lambai ℓ₂) ufuqi rod se latke hain. Aik aur pendulum P bhi latka hai jis ki lambai ℓ₁ ya ℓ₂ ki ja sakti hai. P (lambai ℓ₁) ko jhulaayein to us ki vibration rod ke zariye sab tak pohnchti hai. A aur B ki lambai aur natural frequency P jaisi hai, is liye un ka amplitude barhta hai: resonance. C aur D ki natural frequency mukhtalif hai, woh taqreeban ruke rehte hain. P ki lambai ℓ₂ ho to C aur D resonate karte hain aur A, B ruke rehte hain.

Microwave oven: taqreeban 2.45 GHz (wavelength taqreeban 12 cm) ki microwaves khaane ke paani ke molecules ko hilaati hain; molecules usi frequency par oscillate karte aur takraate hain, aur friction un ki kinetic energy ko heat mein badalti hai. Paani ke baghair bartan garam nahi hote.

Radio tuning: knob ghumaane se receiver circuit ki natural frequency badalti hai. Jab yeh station ki transmission frequency ke barabar ho to resonance hoti hai aur receiver us station ke signal se zyada se zyada energy leta hai; sirf wohi station sunayi deta hai.

Pul: qadam mila kar chalte sipahiyon ke qadmon ki frequency pul ki natural frequency se mil sakti hai; resonance se pul bare amplitude se hil kar gir sakta hai, is liye qadam tor diye jaate hain.

blocks.prompt:
25 Explain the relationship between resonance and standing waves with the help of (i) the Rubens tube (ii) the Chladni plate (iii) acoustic levitation. How does damping affect the sharpness of resonance? (5 marks)
(Resonance aur standing waves ka taalluq (i) Rubens tube (ii) Chladni plate (iii) acoustic levitation ki madad se wazeh karein. Damping resonance ki sharpness par kya asar daalti hai?)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Rubens tube: dhaat ka pipe jis ke oopar suraakh hain aur dono sire band hain; aik sira chhote speaker ya frequency generator se aur doosra jalne wali gas ki supply se juda hai; gas suraakhon se nikal kar jalti hai (Fig. 14.21). Resonance frequency ki aawaz par tube mein standing wave banti hai jis mein zyada aur kam pressure ke points hote hain. Zyada pressure par zyada gas nikalti hai (ooche shole), kam pressure par kam (neeche shole). Ooche shole har pressure antinode par aadhi wavelength ke faasle par hote hain; yun shole nodes aur antinodes dikhate hain.

(ii) Chladni plate: gol ya chaukor dhaat ki plate jo vibrator par ufuqi lagi ho aur centre se chalayi jaye. Resonant normal mode ki frequency par sateh par nodes aur antinodes bante hain. Nodes par plate vibrate nahi karti; chhirki hui ret antinodes se saakin nodes par chali jaati hai aur standing wave ka pattern dikhati hai (Fig. 14.22).

(iii) Acoustic levitation: taqatwar ultrasonic waves ke radiation pressure se chhote zarron (styrofoam ke tukre, paani ke qatre) ko gravity ke khilaaf hawa mein rokna. Transducer aawaz reflector ki taraf bhejta hai; aane wali aur palatne wali waves standing wave banati hain jis ke nodes par pressure kam aur antinodes par zyada hota hai. Yeh farq zarron ko oopar dhakelta hai aur nodes par phansa deta hai jo acoustic traps hain (Fig. 14.23).

Resonance ki sharpness: resonant amplitude aur sharpness dono damping par munhasar hain. Damping jitni kam, amplitude utna zyada aur resonance utni sharp; bohat damped system ka resonance curve kaafi chapta hota hai (Fig. 14.20). Maslan barabar size ka lead bob pith ball se kaafi zyada amplitude se resonate karta hai kyun ke hawa ki rukawat pith ball ko zyada damp karti hai.
